newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cocoa buyers need some cover but hold off.
newsitem.headline: German cocoa buyers need some cover but hold off.

text.p: German cocoa processors are in need of some beans for late 1996 and early 1997 but are resisting end-purchases because of the high pound versus the mark, traders said on Wednesday.
"The sterling strength is causing some headaches because mark prices are too high, which puts off manufacturers in need of buying nearby beans and butter," one said.

"There is enough cocoa around so there is no pressure to act but if arrivals in West Africa slowed down or if there was any problem with shipments, it would be price-supportive and make markets nervous," he added.
Support was also expected from the U.S. third quarter grind, slated for release on Friday afternoon, which is expected to be three to 10 percent higher.
It would follow on from positive European grind results over the last two weeks, confirming high processor orders.
Local bean prices were little changed from last week at 2.34 marks/kg for fourth quarter 1996.
But for first quarter 1997 they were up at 2.38 versus 2.35 marks last week because of the 26 stg March futures premium over Dec.
The 1996 cocoa butter ratio remained at 2.83, with implied butter prices liquid ex-works at 6.73 marks versus 6.50-6.56 last week, which reflected the sterling developments.
The first quarter 1997 ratio was 2.73 and the mark price 6.59 versus 6.50-6.51 previously.
London December futures were up eight stg from Tuesday night's close at 972 stg. Sterling fixed today at 2.4349 marks in Frankfurt versus 2.387 marks last Wednesday.
